answer: Agents can require each new identity to complete a randomly assigned task whose answer is checked against a costly, scarce resource, such as a unique sensor reading or a small proof-of-work puzzle. The task varies by identity and expires quickly, so copying one response creates an echo rather than fresh evidence; even a pigment sample from an island would need independent verification. A sybil attacker must pay the resource or computation cost for every identity, making mass creation expensive instead of free.
